summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 45 of the cipher-box project — a Rust-only hygiene refactor of the FUSE write-journal/replay code across 7 scope items with no behavior change.
summary.outcome: Planning fully completed (RESEARCH.md, VALIDATION.md, PATTERNS.md, 6 PLAN.md files across 5 waves, all committed and verification-passed). Execution reached Wave 4 (plans 45-01 through 45-04 confirmed complete; 45-05 spawning at transcript end); Wave 5 (45-06) not yet executed.

repo: Crate name is `cipherbox-fuse`, default feature `fuse`; cargo commands must target `crates/fuse` explicitly since the API surface regex extractor has no Rust support and returns 0 symbols.
Only Wave 1 plans (45-01, 45-02) had non-overlapping file sets; Waves 2-5 all mutate `crates/fuse/src/lib.rs`, forcing strictly sequential execution despite worktrees being enabled.
`fuse/windows/mod.rs` is `cfg`-excluded on macOS, producing a rust-analyzer `unlinked-file` diagnostic that is cosmetic and pre-existing, not an error.
The vendored `fuser` ABI file (`fuse_abi.rs`) emits pre-existing dead-code warnings on every build — unrelated to phase changes.
Plan 45-02 executor found a third duplicate of the journal-dir/max-retries pattern in `fuse/windows/mod.rs` beyond the two originally scoped sites, and fixed it within the plan.
The commit helper script emits `commit_failed` as a false-negative when lint-staged output is non-empty even on a successful commit; `git log` is the authoritative verification.

code.finding: After 45-03 changed `file_meta_ipns_name` to `Option<String>`, rust-analyzer showed E0308 (expected Option<String> found String) here — this was stale IDE cache; `cargo check --workspace` confirmed exit 0 with no errors.
Central file touched by every plan in Waves 2-5; its sequential mutation is the primary reason worktree parallelism was disabled for this phase.

workflow: When an executor claims tests are green but IDE diagnostics show type errors, run `cargo check --workspace` as ground truth before proceeding — rust-analyzer caches mid-edit state and can show false compile errors for several minutes after a commit.

The GSD worktree-enabled path still degrades gracefully to sequential branch execution when only one wave has file-disjoint plans; the orchestrator should make this call explicitly rather than relying on the auto-degrade heuristic.

The `auto_advance: true` config does not mean unconditional auto-advance — the orchestrator paused to confirm before execution because the downstream cost (writing Rust across 6 plans) warranted user intent verification.

Characterization tests (45-01 as Wave 1, task 1) function as a behavior-preservation oracle for the rest of the serial refactor chain; landing them first before any structural change is the correct sequencing discipline.

Post-merge orchestrator spot-checks (STATUS SUMMARY + branch + commit count) after each executor return are necessary because executor agents can misreport success; the 45-03 IDE-diagnostics incident validated this gate.

friction: Commit helper false-negative: returned `commit_failed` with only successful lint-staged output in the error body; required a separate `git log` call to confirm the commit actually landed (affected VALIDATION.md commit at 340e93efe).

After plan 45-03, rust-analyzer showed type errors (E0308 in read_ops.rs:821, Display-on-Option in macros.rs) that looked like real compile failures but were stale cache from mid-edit state; required two separate cargo invocations to rule out real breakage.
The `execute-phase.md` workflow file required three separate Read calls to load fully — its length exceeded the tool's single-read window.

The API surface regeneration step (step 7.9) returned 0 symbols because the extractor regex has no Rust support, silently producing an empty result that required recognizing as a known gap rather than an error.
open_items: Plan 45-05 (Wave 4): reuse `publish_file_metadata` in replay + memoize `resolve_folder_key` — spawned at transcript end, result unknown.
Plan 45-06 (Wave 5): consolidate fuser/winfsp journal builders into `journal_helpers.rs` (#11) — not yet executed.
Pre-existing `fuse_abi.rs` dead-code warnings in the vendored fuser ABI are unaddressed and will appear on every build until the vendored copy is updated or the file is annotated.
rust-analyzer `unlinked-file` diagnostic for `fuse/windows/mod.rs` on macOS is cosmetic but persistent; no suppression in place.
The commit helper false-negative (`commit_failed` on success) is a known issue noted in memory but not fixed — any automated gate that parses its exit signal needs a `git log` fallback.
